To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of all-cause mortality was high among people living with HIV in Ontario.

the mortality rate of 11.3 deaths per thousand person-years was substantially higher than the mortality rate of the general Canadian population (4.3 deaths per one thousand population) and the rate of 6.8 deaths per thousand population among the general population in Ontario.
homelessness and incarceration independently predict high risk of mortality and suboptimal selfrated general health at previous study visit predicted greater risk of mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social determinants of mortality among PLWH in Ontario.
the social determinants of HIV/AIDS.
the social determinants of HIV/AIDS and their relationship to health outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

social determinants of homelessness and incarceration were independently associated with mortality among MSM and suboptimal self-reported health was a predictor of mortality among MSM and heterosexual men.

the social determinants of HIV disease progression and death in people living with HIV in Canada is a complex interaction of factors, including the individual's own social determinants and their ability to navigate the healthcare system.
social determinants of mortality among PLWHA in Ontario include: (1) homelessness, (2) incarceration, and (3) suboptimal self-reported general health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social determinants of HIV disease progression and associated mortality are important in people living with HIV in Ontario.
the social determinants of mortality among people with HIV/AIDS are not well understood.
we found that people living with HIV in Ontario have high rates of mortality and that the social determinants of mortality are different for MSM and women.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people who are homeless and incarcerated are at increased risk of dying from any cause.
people living with HIV in Ontario are at high risk of premature death.
social determinants are important in the lives of people living with HIV and that they are also associated with mortality.
